task_name: Ironline Forge - Blacksmith editorial image set
client_brief:
Foundry photographs for architects: one dark treatment, visible material

The furnace and rooflight give us two very different versions of Ironline Forge. We need an experienced retoucher to bring them together for architectural audiences and the expo.

Final handoff

 Architectural foundry editorial feature: 1 named export. The sequence explains the foundry's casting work. Tool and material detail remains credible.

 Foundry exhibition poster: 1 named export. The architectural casting offer uses approved copy. The specifier contact is readable.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A heritage iron and bronze foundry casting bespoke architectural work for specifiers and developers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Casting since 1911 in the same Sheffield works; a small crew of founders, patternmakers and finishers.
brand_identity.about: Ironline Forge casts bespoke iron and bronze for architects and developers who have mostly never stood on a foundry floor. We sell permanence and provenance: the heat, the hands, and the fact that the piece will still be here in eighty years. The brand has to feel like the shop floor, hot, dirty and precise.
brand_identity.audience: Specifiers, architects and developers, 40 to 65, buying craft and confidence rather than a catalogue product.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bespoke castings from five to sixty thousand dollars a piece, priced on provenance and never presented as a promotion.
brand_identity.typography: A generous editorial serif for headlines with plenty of black around it, and a strong grotesque for labels and spec lines. Numbers are set plainly.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, declarative, unshowy. Example line: 'Iron and bronze, cast in this building since 1911.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our maker's mark was cut into a die generations ago and survives only struck into the metal. There is no artwork for it anywhere, and the trade-fair stand and the brand story page are being rebuilt at the same time.
brand_identity.values: Process and provenance over polish. The struck maker's mark must be recovered faithfully rather than tidied into a fashion monoline, and it has to hold small and reversed out of the dark.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
